title: Chapter 86: Core of the Truehearted 8
content:
Chapter 86

Core of the Truehearted 8

Wei Wuxian tilted his head. "So, about everything you just claimed—got any actual proof to back it up?"

"None," Sisi admitted flatly.

Sect Leader Yao didn't miss a beat, cutting in immediately: "She laid out every single detail down to the bone! There's no way she's lying!"

Lan Qiren's brow furrowed deep. Turning his sharp gaze toward the other woman, he remarked, "I believe I've seen you before."

Panic flickered across her features. "You... you likely have, sir."

A puzzled murmur rippled through the onlookers. Sisi was an unregistered street prostitute—could this other woman be from the brothels, too? What business would someone as upright as Lan Qiren have ever running into her?

The woman explained, "Whenever the Leling Qin Sect hosted discussion conferences, I was always at my lady's side."

"The Leling Qin Sect?" a female cultivator chimed in. "You're a maidservant from the Qin clan?"

A sharper pair of eyes picked her out instantly: "Wait, you're... Bicao! Madame Qin's personal maid, Bicao! Isn't that right?"

The "Madame Qin" she meant was Qin Cangye's wife—the biological mother of Qin Su, Jin Guangyao’s lady. The woman nodded, her voice hushed. "I am. Though I left the Qin family's service some time ago."

Sect Leader Yao practically bounced out of his seat, slamming a hand onto the table. "Do you have something to tell us as well?"

Bicao’s eyes rimmed with red. "What I have to share happened even earlier. Twelve, maybe thirteen years ago.

"I served my lady for decades and watched our young mistress grow up from a baby. My lady doted on her endlessly, but right before the wedding, her mood completely shifted. Every night she had nightmares, and during the day, she’d burst into tears out of nowhere. I thought it was just a mother's heartache over seeing her daughter marry out. I kept reassuring her, saying the man Miss was marrying—Lianfang-zun, Jin Guangyao—was young, capable, gentle, attentive, and devoted to a fault. I told her the young mistress would be cherished. But the more I tried to comfort her, the more miserable she became.

"Right before the wedding date, my lady came to me late one evening and said she had to see her daughter’s betrothed right then, and that I had to escort her in secret. I told her she could simply summon him, asking why a noble lady would sneak out in the dead of night to visit a young man. If anyone found out, the rumors would ruin her! But she was dead set on going, so I had no choice but to follow. Once we arrived, though, she made me stand guard outside. I didn't hear a single word. I had no idea what she told Jin Guangyao.

"A few days later, the wedding date was set in stone. The moment my lady saw the invitation, she fainted dead away. Even after the wedding went through, she sank into a depression, brooding herself sick. Her health went downhill fast. Right before she drew her final breath, she couldn't carry the weight alone anymore... and told me everything."

Tears spilled down Bicao's cheeks as she choked out the words: "Lianfang-zun, Jin Guangyao, and our young mistress, Qin Su... they weren't husband and wife at all. They were brother and sister..."

"What?!"

If a bolt of divine lightning had torn through the ceiling of the Sword Testing Hall, it couldn't have shattered the room more violently. Across Wei Wuxian's mind flashed the memory of Qin Su's pale, haunted face.

Bicao wept, "My poor lady had the most tragic life... That old beast, Sect Leader Jin, wasn't human! He took a lustful eye to my lady’s looks, caught her alone while he was drunk, and forced himself on her... How could my lady have fought him off? She didn't dare breathe a word of it afterward. My master was fiercely loyal to Jin Guangshan, and she was petrified of what would happen. Jin Guangshan sired so many bastards he couldn't keep track of whose child was whose, but my lady never forgot. She didn't dare confront him. Knowing her daughter was deeply in love with Jin Guangyao, she agonized over it until she finally snuck out before the wedding, confiding the truth to Jin Guangyao and begging him to call it off before a catastrophic sin was committed. But who would have guessed... who could have imagined that knowing full well Qin Su was his own flesh-and-blood half-sister, Jin Guangyao went ahead and married her anyway!"

And worse than simply taking her hand—they had consummated the union and had a child together!

A horrifying, unprecedented scandal of the highest order!

The hall erupted in a deafening roar of outrage, voices cascading over one another:

"Old Sect Leader Qin served by Jin Guangshan's side for decades! To violate the wife of your most loyal subordinate—that wretched dog, Jin Guangshan!"

"The truth always finds a way out in the end..."

"Jin Guangyao needed a solid foothold in the Lanling Jin Sect, and having Qin Cangye as a staunch father-in-law was the only way to secure it. How could he ever bear to walk away from that kind of leverage?"

"When it comes to pure depravity, the man is truly in a league of his own!"

Wei Wuxian leaned in close, murmuring to Lan Wangji, "No wonder he told Qin Su in that secret chamber that A-Song had to die."

Others in the hall quickly made the connection. Sect Leader Yao spoke up, "Looking at it this way, I’d venture a bold guess: his son was never murdered by enemies. Jin Guangyao poisoned the boy himself!"

"What makes you say that?" someone asked.

Sect Leader Yao laid it out with smug authority: "Children born of incestuous blood between siblings are almost always born dim-witted. Jin Rusong was only a few years old when he died, right around the age a child begins their basic schooling. When they're toddlers, you can't tell if something's wrong, but the older they get, the harder it is to hide that the child isn't right in the head. Even if people didn't suspect incest, siring an idiot son would have dragged Jin Guangyao through the mud. People would have whispered behind his back, sneering that his prostitute mother's dirty blood was tainting the lineage..."

A chorus of nodding heads rippled through the crowd. "Sect Leader Yao's deduction is razor-sharp!"

Sect Leader Yao pressed on, "And to make it even more obvious, wasn't the man framed for poisoning Jin Rusong the very clan leader who opposed building those watchtowers? Since when does the world hand out coincidences that neat?" He let out a cold sneer. "Either way, Jin Guangyao had zero use for a defective son. Murdering Jin Rusong, pinning it on his political rival, and then launching a righteous crusade against the dissenting clan under the noble banner of avenging his dead child—it was cold-blooded butchery, but it killed two birds with one stone. Lianfang-zun certainly plays a ruthless hand!"

Wei Wuxian turned his gaze back onto Bicao. "The night of the discussion conference at Koi Tower—did you meet with Qin Su?"

Bicao stiffened.

Wei Wuxian pressed, "That night, inside the Fragrance Palace, Qin Su had a bitter screaming match with Jin Guangyao. She said she went to meet someone who revealed the truth to her and gave her a letter, swearing this person would never lie to her. Was that person you?"

Bicao swallowed. "...It was."

"You guarded this secret for over a decade," Wei Wuxian said, studying her face. "Why break your silence now? And why choose this exact moment to drag it all into the open?"

"Because..." Bicao stammered, "because I had to make my young mistress see what kind of monster she was sleeping beside! I never intended to make it a public spectacle, but then my lady took her own life on Koi Tower out of nowhere! I have to strip away that hypocrite's mask! I have to get justice for my mistress and her mother!"

A faint, hollow smile touched Wei Wuxian's lips. "Haven't you figured it out yet? The only reason your young mistress took her own life out of nowhere was because you told her."

Bicao gasped, "I..."

Sect Leader Yao frowned, cutting in with annoyance: "I have to disagree with you there! Are you saying keeping people in the dark was the right call?"

A bystander immediately chimed in, "You can't blame her! Ah, Madame Ji—er, Qin Su was simply far too fragile."

Several senior female cultivators murmured in sympathy: "Poor Qin Su, what a tragedy."

"To think I actually envied her back then! Good birth, an enviable marriage, the undisputed mistress of Koi Tower with a husband devoted only to her... and to think, tsk tsk."

An elder noblewoman offered an airy, philosophical sigh: "It just goes to show: the most dazzling things on the surface are usually rotting with a hundred holes underneath. There was never anything to envy."

Wei Wuxian thought to himself, Qin Su probably chose to end it all because she couldn't bear the thought of listening to this exact brand of gossip—people pretending to pity her while chewing on her tragedy like delicious candy.

He glanced down and caught sight of a piece of jewelry resting against Bicao's wrist—an exquisite bangle of pure emerald-green jade wrapped in fine gold. The craftsmanship was stunning, far beyond anything a common maid could ever dream of affording.

Smiling faintly, he murmured, "Nice bracelet."

Bicao jerked her sleeve down in a panic, ducking her head in silence.

Nie Huaisang blinked, piping up with wide-eyed innocence: "B-But... who on earth sent these two women here today?"

Sect Leader Yao waved it off impatiently. "Why waste energy fretting over that?! Whoever it is, one thing is set in stone: the man is a righteous hero, and he's firmly on our side!"

A wave of agreement washed through the room: "Hear, hear!"

Wei Wuxian, however, wasn't sold. "Whoever broke Sisi out certainly isn't an amateur. He’s got deep pockets and plenty of time on his hands. But calling him a righteous hero? That’s jumping the gun."

Lan Wangji added softly, "Too many suspicious threads."

Coming from Wei Wuxian, the warning would have been dismissed as white noise. But coming from Lan Wangji, the room instantly swallowed its chatter.

Lan Qiren asked, "Where do the suspicions lie?"

"Where don't they?" Wei Wuxian replied smoothly. "Take Jin Guangyao: if he’s truly that ruthless, why butcher twenty courtesans only to leave Sisi breathing? We have living witnesses today, sure—but where's the physical proof?"

His constant pushback was like a splash of cold water over their righteous frenzy, rubbing several clan leaders the wrong way. Sect Leader Yao barked back, "The net of heaven has large meshes, yet nothing slips through! Justice catches up eventually!"

Hearing that, Wei Wuxian merely smiled and let the topic drop.

He knew nobody in this room had the patience to listen to him, let alone weigh his doubts with a clear head. Pushing further would only paint a target on his own back. A decade ago, he wouldn't have given a damn about their fragile egos; he would've spoken his mind and shoved the truth down their throats whether they liked it or not. But today, Wei Wuxian had zero interest in stealing the spotlight.

And right on cue, the room erupted into an escalating crescendo of furious condemnation:

"To think a man could be this ungrateful and depraved!"

Hearing "ungrateful" and "depraved" hurled across the room gave Wei Wuxian an instinctive jolt—for thirteen years, those two labels had been practically glued to his own forehead. For a second, he thought they were yelling at him again. The same people doing the screaming, the exact same slurs being thrown around—only the target had shifted. It was an odd, disorienting sensation.

Another cultivator chimed in with righteous venom: "Back then, Jin Guangyao clawed his way to the top purely by groveling at the feet of Chifeng-zun and Ze-wu-jun! How else could the son of a whore have ever sat upon that throne? And to turn around and butcher Chifeng-zun in cold blood! Ze-wu-jun is still in his clutches right now—heaven pray nothing has happened to him!"

Only an hour ago, these very men had laughed off the idea that Nie Mingjue’s death, the dismemberment of his corpse, and the ambush at the Burial Mounds were tied to Jin Guangyao. Now, they bought every single word as gospel.

"Not just his sworn brothers—his own flesh and blood couldn't escape his knife either! During Jin Guangshan's final years, he ran around hunting down every bastard his old man ever sired, petrified someone would challenge his claim. Mo Xuanyu got off lucky; if he hadn't gone mad and gotten kicked out, he would’ve vanished off the map just like the rest of them."

"Jin Zixuan's death definitely had his fingerprints on it, too!"

"Who remembers Daozhang Xiao Xingchen? 'The bright moon and gentle breeze, Xiao Xingchen.' And the slaughter of the Chang Clan of Yueyang! Xue Yang was kept alive and sheltered entirely thanks to Lianfang-zun!"

"Right! When Daozhang Xiao Xingchen first descended from the mountain, didn't half the prominent clans try to recruit him as a guest elder? The Lanling Jin Sect extended an invitation too, but he politely turned them down. The Jins were strutting around at their peak back then; getting snubbed by a wandering rogue stung their pride, so protecting Xue Yang later was partly settling that petty old grudge! They just wanted to see Xiao Xingchen crushed!"

"Disgraceful! Who do the Jins think they are? Spurn their banner and they ruin your life?!"

"Such a tragedy, truly. I had the privilege of witnessing Daozhang Xiao Xingchen hunt in his prime. Shuanghua's blade once moved the entire world."

"And then Jin Guangyao cleaned house and disposed of Xue Yang later anyway—dog eat dog, through and through!"

"I heard that back when Jin Guangyao was an undercover mole in the Qishan Wen Sect, he was playing both sides! His plan was simple: if the Sunshot Campaign went south, he'd stay in Qishan and lick Wen Ruohan's boots like a loyal lapdog. But if the Wen Clan crumbled, he'd turn his blade around and play the war hero!"

"Wen Ruohan must be rolling in his grave right now—he raised Jin Guangyao as his personal protégé! Seventy to eighty percent of Jin Guangyao's swordplay was taught to him by Wen Ruohan's own hand!"

"That's nothing! I heard the only reason Chifeng-zun's surprise raid failed back then was because Jin Guangyao fed him false intelligence on purpose!"

"Let me throw another secret onto the pile: all that gold and materials for the watchtowers—wasn't it squeezed out of our pockets? Every clan bled to contribute, and I heard he quietly skimmed... this much right off the top!"

"Good heavens... that much?! Shameless scoundrel! To think I actually thought he was working for the common good—our goodwill was fed to a pack of rabid dogs!"

Wei Wuxian watched the circus, feeling a dry, cynical amusement rising in his chest. If it's just a rumor, why swallow it so eagerly? And if it's a secret, how the hell do all of you seem to know it?

These whispers hadn't surfaced yesterday; they had been circulating for years. But back when Jin Guangyao sat unchallenged at the pinnacle of power, the gossip had been tightly muzzled, laughed off as jealous fabrications. Tonight, however, every idle rumor had solidified into unshakeable, ironclad fact—paving the foundation of his monstrous crimes, used to prove just how irredeemably rotten he had always been.

"When you lay it all out, this Jin scoundrel has killed his father, killed his brother, killed his wife, killed his son, killed his master, killed his friend... and committed incest to boot! An absolute, terrifying fiend!"

"The Lanling Jin Sect has always been an overbearing bully, and Jin Guangyao ruled with an iron fist, never listening to a single word of counsel! The rampant decadence, corruption, and tyranny choking the cultivation world today was bred entirely by his hand! Did he honestly think we would swallow this abuse forever?!"

"He watched our clans grow stronger over the years, felt threatened by our rising power, and panicked that he'd end up overthrown just like the Qishan Wen Sect! That's why he decided to wipe us all out in one fell swoop!"

Sect Leader Yao let out a venomous sneer. "In that case, let us make his worst nightmare come true!" He slammed his palm against the tabletop. "We march on Koi Tower!"

Amidst the roaring cheers and table-slapping approvals shaking the hall, Wei Wuxian thought quietly: Barely a few hours ago, this terrifying fiend was still the universally adored Lianfang-zun. One night, and the entire world is screaming for his head.

Suddenly, a voice piped up beside him: "Master Wei, that scoundrel Jin Guangyao has the Yin Tiger Tally in his grip. When the time comes, we will be counting on you!"

Wei Wuxian blinked, startled. "Huh?"

He genuinely hadn't expected anyone to address him willingly—let alone with such beaming warmth, going so far as to call him "Master" instead of spitting "Wei-dog" or "heretic." Before he could process it, another clan leader chimed in, grinning broadly: "Indeed! When it comes to mastering the dark path, no one can rival the great Yiling Laozu!"

"This time, Jin Guangyao has kicked an iron plate, haha!"

Wei Wuxian was thoroughly at a loss for words. The last time the cultivation world had fawned over him like this was during the Sunshot Campaign over a decade ago. While he had finally lived long enough to watch someone else take his seat as Public Enemy Number One, the taste in his mouth wasn't sweet, and he felt zero moving warmth at being "accepted" by the world again. In fact, a quiet, cynical doubt wormed its way into his thoughts: Back then... did they also gather in some secret hall just like this, cursing my name to the heavens, before deciding to siege the Burial Mounds?

By the time the council wrapped up, the banquet prepared by the Yunmeng Jiang Sect was set and ready. Yet when the guests took their seats, two figures were conspicuously missing.

A clan leader frowned, looking around. "Where are... er, where are the Yiling Laozu and Hanguang-jun?"

Seated at the head of the hall, Jiang Cheng turned to his retainer. "Where did they go?"

The attendant bowed low. "The two gentlemen changed their robes after leaving the hall, saying they would skip the banquet to take a walk outside, and would return shortly."

Jiang Cheng let out an icy sneer. "Same as always. Zero manners."

The barb lumped Lan Wangji into the insult as well, earning an immediate scowl from Lan Qiren. If Lan Wangji was lacking in manners, then basic human decency didn't exist under the heavens. Thinking about who was dragging his prized nephew into the mud, Lan Qiren ground his teeth at the thought of Wei Wuxian all over again.

Down on the dais, Jiang Cheng smoothed his expression, offering a stiff, polite nod to his guests. "Please, help yourselves. I shall personally fetch them in a moment."

Outside Lotus Pier, along the riverbanks by the docks, Lan Wangji strolled in unhurried, companionable silence, letting Wei Wuxian lead the way without asking a single question about their destination.

A few late-night street stalls were still operating along the water. Wei Wuxian drifted toward one, his face lighting up. "Skipping that stuffy banquet was definitely the right call! Lan Zhan, come here, look—these flatbreads are incredible! My treat! Boss, two, please!"

The vendor broke into a broad grin, wrapping two steaming pastries in brown paper. Wei Wuxian reached out to take them, only to freeze mid-motion as reality caught up with him: he didn't have a single copper coin to his name. How was he supposed to treat anyone?

Before the awkwardness could settle, Lan Wangji stepped in smoothly, accepting the paper-wrapped pastries with one hand while tossing a silver coin with the other.

Wei Wuxian rubbed the back of his neck, sheepish. "Ah... my bad. Why does this always happen? Seems like every single time I promise to treat you to food, you end up footing the bill."

"It does not matter," Lan Wangji murmured.

Wei Wuxian took a generous bite, chewing happily. "Back in the day, I never paid for food around these docks. Whatever I wanted, I grabbed and ate on the go! A month later, the vendor would just stroll up to Lotus Pier and bill Uncle Jiang for the tab."

Lan Wangji took a small, delicate crescent out of his own flatbread, his tone quiet and even. "You do not need to pay now, either."

Wei Wuxian burst into uproarious, delighted laughter.

He inhaled the rest of the bread in three bites, crumpling the greasy wrapper into a little ball and tossing it lightly between his hands. Scanning the quiet shore, he sighed softly. "Not many stalls left, huh? Back then, no matter how late it got, this pier was packed with vendors hawking all kinds of midnight snacks. The disciples at Lotus Pier loved sneaking out for late-night bites. Boats lined the water for miles—it was every bit as lively as your Caiyi Town."

He trailed off, his voice dipping with fond melancholy. "There’s so little of it left now. Lan Zhan, you arrived too late. You missed this place when it was at its finest, at its most lively."

Lan Wangji looked at him. "Not late."

Wei Wuxian smiled, turning to face him. "Back when we were studying at the Cloud Recesses, I invited you to Yunmeng so many times, but you completely ignored me. I should’ve been pushier back then—should’ve just dragged you here kicking and screaming. Hey, why are you eating so slow? Is it bad?"

"Do not speak while eating," Lan Wangji replied.

He had always chewed his food thoroughly and deliberately, adhering strictly to the rule that if words had to be exchanged, not a single scrap of food could remain in his mouth.

Wei Wuxian chuckled, "Fine, fine, I won't distract you. Eat up. I thought you hated it; was about to offer to finish the rest for you."

Lan Wangji turned toward the stall vendor. "Another portion, please."

By the time Wei Wuxian had polished off his third flatbread, Lan Wangji was still nibbling his way through his first. Following Wei Wuxian’s lead, their footsteps carried them further and further from the gates of Lotus Pier, Wei Wuxian animatedly pointing out landmarks along the path.

He desperately wanted to show Lan Wangji every single corner where he had grown up, played, and raised hell—telling him about every prank he’d pulled, every fistfight he’d scrapped in, every wild pheasant he’d chased through the brush. And through it all, he watched Lan Wangji’s quiet profile, hanging on every tiny shift in his expression.

"Lan Zhan!" Wei Wuxian called out, turning around. "Look at me. Look at this tree."

Lan Wangji had finally finished his pastry, folding the brown paper into an immaculate, tiny square between his fingers. He lifted his gaze toward where Wei Wuxian was pointing.

It was an ordinary tree, straight-trunked with sweeping branches, likely several decades old. Wei Wuxian strolled over, circling the trunk twice before giving the rough bark an affectionate slap.

"I climbed this tree once."

Lan Wangji remarked dryly, "On the way here, you claimed to have climbed every single tree we passed."

"This one is different!" Wei Wuxian protested, beaming. "This was the very first tree I ever climbed after coming to Lotus Pier! Dead of night, too. My Shijie came out looking for me carrying a paper lantern, terrified I was going to fall, standing right beneath the branches with her arms outstretched to catch me. But her little arms were so thin—how could she have caught a whole boy? I ended up snapping a leg anyway."

Lan Wangji’s gaze dipped down to his legs. "Why climb a tree in the middle of the night?"

Wei Wuxian leaned forward with an easy, laughing grin. "No reason! You know me—I've always loved sneaking out to cause trouble after dark. Haha."
